extracted.intended_audience: students and readers of philosophy; writers or theorists interested in Bergson's ideas about time, life, and creativity
extracted.subtask_description: Extracts of Henri Bergson's Creative Evolution presenting philosophical criteria about duration, novelty, and living change that can inform creative practice and theory. Focuses on how life, memory, and time relate to the production of new forms.

rubrics_metrics.name: Duration as creative principle
rubrics_metrics.description: "The universe endures. . . duration means invention, the creation of forms, the continual elaboration of the absolutely new."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Creative work should embody a sense of duration — an ongoing process of invention rather than static representation. Bergson uses examples (waiting for sugar to dissolve) to show that lived time is the medium in which forms are created; writers should represent processes that unfold and generate novelty rather than merely depict fixed states.

rubrics_metrics.name: Originality / unforeseeability of new forms
rubrics_metrics.description: "The more we fix our attention on this continuity of life, the more we see that organic evolution resembles the evolution of a consciousness, in which the past presses against the present and causes the upspringing of a new form of consciousness, incommensurable with its antecedents."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Art should aim to produce forms that are not fully predictable from antecedent elements. Bergson insists that genuine creation issues something unforeseeable; as a criterion, a strong creative work introduces incommensurable, genuinely new developments rather than merely recombining familiar elements in obvious ways.

rubrics_metrics.name: Integration of memory / persistence of past in the present
rubrics_metrics.description: "The very basis of our conscious existence is memory, that is to say, the prolongation of the past into the present, or, in a word, duration, acting and irreversible."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Good creative practice shows how characters, settings, and forms carry their past persistently into the present moment. Rather than treating scenes or moments as isolated, narratively layer prior events, habits, and accumulations so the present appears as an effect of an irretrievable past.

rubrics_metrics.name: Reject mechanistic / purely mathematical explanations
rubrics_metrics.description: "It is of the very essence of mechanism... to consider as metaphorical every expression which attributes to time an effective action and a reality of its own."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Avoid reducing life and narrative to mere mechanical rearrangements or to clock-time causality. Anti-pattern: treating characters as if their present were explained solely by the immediately preceding instant (the 'hour-glass' or purely differential-equation view). Instead, represent organic, irreversible processes that cannot be exhausted by mechanistic accounts.

rubrics_metrics.name: Emphasize lived/subjective time over abstract/mathematical time
rubrics_metrics.description: "The world the mathematician deals with is a world that dies and is reborn at every instant... To know a living being or natural system is to get at the very interval of duration, while the knowledge of an artificial or mathematical system applies only to the extremity."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Narrative techniques should capture the flow and continuity of subjective time (the 'hyphen' connecting past and present) rather than only a succession of discrete instants. Use interiority, temporal layering, and pacing that reflect ongoing becoming rather than merely chronicle events in inert sequence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Depict gradual maturation leading to apparent sudden change
rubrics_metrics.description: "Even the sudden 'mutations'... are possible only if a process of incubation, or rather of maturing, is going on throughout a series of generations that do not seem to change."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Portray major shifts (plot twists, character transformations) as the culmination of long, often imperceptible processes. Sudden events should be grounded in prior incubation—accumulate small signs and tendencies so abrupt changes feel organic rather than arbitrary.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resist the intellect's bias for repetition and predictability
rubrics_metrics.description: "Intellect therefore instinctively selects in a given situation whatever is like something already known; it seeks this out, in order that it may apply its principle that 'like produces like.'... Science... is concerned only with the aspect of repetition."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Be mindful that cognitive habits favor repetition and recognizable patterns; as a creative criterion, work should consciously challenge this bias, avoiding overreliance on cliché, formulaic plots, or easy analogies that simply reenact known patterns. Philosophy/art must attend to irreducibility.

rubrics_metrics.name: Portray individuality as tendency and incompleteness
rubrics_metrics.description: "Individuality admits of any number of degrees, and that it is not fully realized anywhere... vital properties are never entirely realized, though always on the way to become so; they are not so much states as tendencies."
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Characterization should favor processual, in-progress identities over fully closed, static archetypes. Treat individuality as a set of tendencies and contradictions (e.g., the tension between individuation and reproduction) rather than as a fixed, completed essence.

rubrics_metrics.name: Show interconnectedness between organisms/systems and their whole
rubrics_metrics.description: Objects and isolated systems are abstractions cut out by perception, whereas the living body is bound up with the rest of the universe; isolation is never complete and threads bind systems together.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Place characters and scenes within larger networks and contexts; avoid depicting entities as ontologically self-sufficient. Use details that indicate external influences, environmental continuities, and systemic ties so that the narrative reflects the organism's embeddedness in a wider whole.
